Keeps Samuel’s breakers rather than the parallel psalm’s cords at this point.
Retains Sheol and the distinct cords and traps.
Follows read shaking and retains foundations of heaven rather than mountains from the parallel psalm.
Retains pinned appeared rather than importing soared from Psalm 18.
Preserves plural shelters and the difficult gathered-water image.
Follows the read verb while retaining the implied targets and lightning parallel.
Preserves the speaker’s claim and embodied clean hands without harmonizing the narrative’s moral tensions.
Follows read plural judgments and retains both law terms.
Keeps blameless and personal guilt rather than weakening either claim.
Preserves the refrain’s variation: this verse does not repeat hands.
Retains the reciprocal word pattern and Samuel’s warrior wording.
Keeps contrasting responses without flattening the difficult second verb into simple opposition.
Preserves complete way, metal-testing image, and refuge refrain.

Follows read my feet and retains the female deer comparison and high places.
Retains a defensible answering sense of the difficult noun rather than silently substituting Psalm 18’s form.
Keeps the violence and relentless pursuit in the song’s own voice.
Retains repeated finishing and the enemies underfoot.
Preserves the backs image of flight and explicit destruction.
Retains pinned looking rather than changing it to crying out from the parallel psalm.
Keeps all three violent actions and both material comparisons.
Keeps the compelled or feigned submission sense and immediate hearing.
Uses the possible faltering sense of the difficult verb; its relation to girding requires a note.
Keeps vengeance and political subjection explicit; the sentence continues.
